add.title: Permanent hostname: one step is yours
add.text: You asked for a permanent address. Your Cloudflare account holds lew42.com, so the plan is a named tunnel at **servex.lew42.com** (the connector URL then never changes). The build stopped at one thing: the saved API token has no DNS permission. **Your step:** in the Cloudflare dashboard, edit that API token and add *Zone → DNS → Edit* for lew42.com (or add the CNAME by hand later). Then say "build the permanent tunnel" and an agent finishes it. Steps and detail: /Servex/ext/remote/doc/tunnel.md. Meanwhile Servex now keeps the quick tunnel alive by itself, and the current host is shown in handover.md; paste today's URL from remote.url into the connector once.

add.title: Permanent URL is blocked on two token permissions
add.text: The Cloudflare API token in cloudflare.env can only list. Add **Account → Cloudflare Tunnel → Edit** and **Zone → DNS → Edit** (lew42.com), then run `node Server/TunnelNamed.mjs setup`, `node Server/Tunnel.mjs down`, `node Server/Tunnel.mjs up`. After that, paste https://servex.lew42.com/mcp/remote/<token> (token in remote.url) into the connector once; it never changes again. Details: [tunnel.md](/Servex/ext/remote/doc/tunnel.md).

add.title: Done: the permanent connector URL is live
add.text: servex.lew42.com answers at the Cloudflare edge (17:25). Paste https://servex.lew42.com/mcp/remote/<token> into the Claude app's Servex connector once (the token is the same one as always, in %LOCALAPPDATA%\lew42\servex\remote.url). It never changes again: a named tunnel, kept alive by Servex, with the quick tunnel as the fallback if the named token file is ever missing.
